messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] GPU pool saturation: eu-west-1-gpu-pool reported sustained queue growth > 95% for 12m. Autoscaler attempted 3 scale events but failed with provider 429/limit responses. Paging oncall.
ops-oncall (Maya): I'm on it — joining the call now. Can someone post quick impact numbers?
ben-sre: queue depth spike from ~40 -> 980 over 8m. p95 latency for served requests jumped to 3.2s, error rate 502/timeout ~2.1%. We started throttling at 750 queued jobs.
cara-platform: autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts:
```
2026-03-14T21:12:07Z scale_attempt id=zz123 provider_response=429 quota_exceeded
2026-03-14T21:13:12Z scale_attempt id=zz124 provider_response=429 rate_limit
2026-03-14T21:14:59Z scale_attempt id=zz125 provider_response=422 insufficient_capacity
```
ops-oncall (Maya): cause sounds like provider-side rate limits + regional capacity exhaustion. Any active deploys?
frank-eng: no deploys in last 30m. We did roll a new model shard earlier today but it was green.
derek-ml: customer impact: multiple long-lived inference jobs (batch rerank) were queued and timed out. Support ticket volume rising — Emma, can you confirm severity/classification?
emma-support: flagging SEV2 for affected customers in EU with >5% request failures. Noting a few customers reported timeouts and degraded latency on embeddings endpoints.
laura-eng-infra: I'm looking at node boot errors. Some nodes failed to initialize due to kernel module OOM on instance types during provisioning. See snippet:
```
[init] attach_kv_cache failed: out_of_memory
[agent] provider returned 429 on create_instance
```
ben-sre: autoscaler backoff currently configured with exponential backoff up to 10m. Because provider 429s are persistent, our controller gave up after 3 tries (we hit scale limit flag). Need manual mitigation.
ops-oncall (Maya): immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) enable burst capacity in eu-west-1 (if available), 2) divert non-critical traffic to dedicated-gpu-pool-us-east, 3) enable model-fallback to quantized-2g for chat_endpoints to reduce per-request GPU RAM. Who can run each?
cara-platform: I can enable divert for non-critical routes, adding a routing rule in ~2 min. Will annotate traffic in logs.
frank-eng: I can flip the model-fallback toggle and promote a smaller variant for chat endpoints. Rolling in 90s.
laura-eng-infra: Burst capacity request submitted to provider console, status: pending (rate-limited). I will try alternative zone in the region.
ben-sre: I'll start draining batch workers (low-priority) and evict queued background jobs to free slots. We'll return results with 1-2m cadence.
emma-support: notifying affected customers with a short status update: "We're experiencing increased inference latency and timeouts in EU; mitigations in progress — routing and capacity changes being applied. More updates in 30m." :loudspeaker:
ops-oncall (Maya): good. Also set circuit-breaker to reduce concurrent sessions from 8 -> 2 for EU tenants to reduce new queue pressure. Anyone can patch the config?
cara-platform: applying concurrency cap for eu-* routes now. Confirmed: concurrency cap applied at 21:20:42 UTC.
ben-sre: draining low-priority queue: evicted ~430 jobs, freed 32 GPUs (approx). Queue depth dropped to 420. p50 latency improved to 1.3s.
derek-ml: Model-fallback live: traffic moving to quantized-2g for chat. Token-level cost should drop ~3x. Monitoring accuracy regressions async.
laura-eng-infra: alternative zone spin-up succeeded for 6 nodes. Provider still returning occasional 429s but overall capacity increased.
ops-oncall (Maya): good progress. Are there customer-facing throttles still active?
emma-support: still seeing timeouts for a small subset (5 customers) but majority reduced. Escalating the 5 biggest accounts to SEV2 owners.
frank-eng: added temporary rate-limit header guidance in the gateway: `Retry-After` and `x-rw-limited: true` for impacted routes.
ben-sre: confirming autoscaler metrics — attempts resumed and new nodes registered at 21:29:10. We have 64 GPUs online vs 22 at peak queue. Queue draining steadily.
ops-oncall (Maya): let's call a 10m triage bridge to coordinate remaining mitigation steps and timeline for full restoration. Dial-in posted.
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] Severity reduced from P1 -> P2 at 21:36 UTC — queue under control, but customer impact remains for a small segment.
ops-oncall (Maya): postmortem notes to capture: root cause appears to be provider-side rate limiting combined with an earlier kernel OOM that caused a subset of spin-ups to fail which triggered autoscaler to back off and hit our max retries. Key failure modes: 1) insufficient jitter on scale retries, 2) lack of fallback routing for long-running batch jobs, 3) no prioritized eviction policy for mixed-priority queues.
ben-sre: tentative action items: - increase autoscaler max retries and smarter jitter - add exponential backoff with randomized jitter across AZs - add regional fallback routing to dedicated pools - implement background-job preemption policy - improve probe to distinguish provider 429 vs 5xx
cara-platform: I'll own the routing fallback item and add an automated policy to divert non-prod / low-priority traffic to dedicated pools when queue > 70%.
laura-eng-infra: I'll own the infrastructure change: work with provider on OOM root cause, add node initialization retries, and add node-level memory guards to avoid kernel OOMs.
derek-ml: I'll run a targeted eval on quantized-2g for the top 10 customer prompt sets to check for regressions and produce a rollback plan.
emma-support: I'll update the customer comms template and run through impacted-customer list with account teams.
frank-eng: I'll add a gateway enhancement: surface `x-rw-queue-pos` in responses so customers can introspect backlog position.
ops-oncall (Maya): timeline: immediate mitigations done. Medium-term (48-72h): autoscaler config changes + routing fallback. Long-term (2-4 weeks): provider-capacity playbooks + runbook for node OOM patterns.
incident-bot: [ACTION] New action items created and assigned: cara-platform, laura-eng-infra, derek-ml, ben-sre, frank-eng, emma-support.
ops-oncall (Maya): closing post-incident bridge — will draft a postmortem and share early findings in #incidents within 24h. Thanks all for quick response. :heart:
emma-support: posted customer update at 22:05 UTC.
ben-sre: final metrics snapshot at 22:10 UTC — queue depth back to baseline 18, error rate <0.1%. Marking incident as mitigated.
incident-bot: [RESOLVED] Incident resolved at 22:11 UTC.
ops-oncall (Maya): filing the follow-up doc now. We'll keep an eye on eu-west-1 autoscaler anomalies for the next 72h.
